title: Silence
hook: silence makes room for God to speak
tomorrow: Mia's right there. so why does Sofia keep checking her phone?

segments.voice: Yesterday, apology: a son's rehearsed speech that lost its bargaining line once his father ran to him. The line was no excuses.

Sent. Delivered. Read. Then nothing, not even the dots. Silence after something hard can feel like a verdict, and a thumb hovers over the keyboard to fill it. Should she text again? Inside the Church, silence has two schools of thought, and both of them have a case. One says keep it. The other says speak up and sing. It's a question for prayer too: when to talk, and when to wait.
screen: `SENT. DELIVERED. READ.` → `A THUMB OVER THE KEYBOARD.` → `TWO SCHOOLS OF SILENCE.`

segments.voice: The first side says: keep the silence, because that's where God speaks. Elijah, worn out and hiding on the mountain of God, watches a great wind, then an earthquake, then fire, and the Lord is in none of them. Then, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "a whistling of a gentle air." That's when he covers his face and steps out to listen. The Church's instructions for Mass ask for sacred silence at set moments, such as after the readings and after Communion. On this side, silence isn't empty. It's room. Some Catholics love a quiet weekday Mass for exactly this. The second side says: speak up, sing out. The Church's prayer is public, spoken and sung. The Second Vatican Council asked the people at Mass to take part with acclamations, responses, psalms and songs, not to sit there as silent spectators. A faith that never says anything can shrink into something private. Some Catholics love a full choir and a loud Gloria for exactly that. Here's the turn: both views come from the same paragraph. The Council lists the singing and the speaking, and then adds that at the proper times all should keep a reverent silence. Ecclesiastes put it in one line long before: "A time to keep silence, and a time to speak." The argument among Catholics isn't silence against speech. It's which time is now.
screen: `NOT IN THE WIND OR THE FIRE.` · `SACRED SILENCE AT MASS.` · `NO SILENT SPECTATORS.` · `A TIME FOR EACH.` · then, large: `ROOM TO SPEAK.`

segments.voice: Let the next stretch be silence: nothing playing, nothing to read. Listen for the quietest sound in the room, a fan, a clock, your own breathing, and stay with it. If the noise in your head gets loud, let it pass like Elijah's wind. If you pray, you can say Samuel's line once, speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth, and then simply listen.
Silence. Quiet kept on purpose, at the right time, so there's room for someone else to speak.
Your line: room to speak. Elijah heard it only after the wind, the earthquake and the fire had passed. Go quietly.

chat.meaning: Elijah heard the gentle air only after the noise passed. There's a time to keep silence, and it can be room for someone else to speak.

Elijah.meaning: a prophet of Israel who heard God after the storm

Second Vatican Council.meaning: a council of the world's Catholic bishops that renewed the Mass

Ecclesiastes.meaning: a wisdom book of the Bible about life's seasons

Samuel.meaning: a prophet who heard God call him as a boy
